title: Barcelona 3-2 Villarreal: Yamal overcomes missed penalty to star in comeback win
subtitle: Lamine Yamal may have missed a penalty, but he proved to be influential in Barcelona's superb comeback win against Villarreal on Sunday.
paragraphs: Barcelona scored three times in the space of 10 second-half minutes as they came from two goals down to beat Villarreal 3-2 at Camp Nou.
Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a two-goal cushion just seven minutes into Sunday's contest, but LaLiga champions Barca came out fighting after the break.
Hansi Flick's side hit back through Gerard Martin before Lamine Yamal, who had earlier missed a penalty, teed up Fermin Lopez to level things up soon after.
Pau Navarro, who was later sent off, scored an own goal to ensure Barca moved three points clear of Real Madrid at the top of LaLiga.
But Barca were in all sorts of trouble early on, with Buchanan ruthlessly punishing Fermin's sloppy pass into midfield with a superb strike from distance in the fifth minute.
Villarreal doubled up just 128 seconds later. Oluwaseyi broke down the right-hand side before rifling an effort into the roof of the net.
Oluwaseyi then offered Barcelona a way back into the game when he clumsily tripped Yamal, with the decision given after the referee was sent to the pitchside monitor.
Yamal, though, dragged his spot-kick onto the right post.

But Villarreal wilted under Barca's pressure after the break. Peter Gulacsi tipped Joao Cancelo's fierce drive onto the post, with the resulting corner taken short, and Pedri's delivery was delicately flicked home by Martin.
Barca were level four minutes later as Yamal drove at Renato Veiga before squaring for Fermin, who sent a first-time effort into the bottom-right corner.
Yamal was at the centre of things again as Barca went ahead. After turning Sergi Cardona inside out, he back-heeled into the path of Eric Garcia, whose cross was turned into his own net by Navarro.

Fermin seemingly received a red card as he protested a decision from the bench, but Barca's victory was sealed when Navarro's miserable outing was capped off by a red card in second-half stoppage time.
Barcelona's brilliant attack gets makeshift defence out of trouble

Flick was handed a defensive headache with Andreas Christensen ruled out with an injury, while Pau Cubarsi, who sustained a hip issue while on international duty, was only fit enough to feature on the bench.

Barca's back four included Frenkie de Jong starting at centre back, and the Blaugrana were all at sea in the opening seven minutes. It is the first time they have conceded twice that early in a LaLiga match since November 1981 against Real Zaragoza.

However, Yamal was intent on leading the fightback, causing Villarreal all kinds of problems. He recorded team-high totals for shots (eight), successful dribbles (four) and touches in the opposition box (13), and will perhaps be disappointed not to get on the scoresheet.
But he was able to assist Fermin, teeing up his compatriot for the fourth time in all competitions this season.
Fermin has now been involved in 13 goals in 12 games in LaLiga in 2026-27, and his second-half strike was the perfect response to his early error.

Villarreal coach Inigo Perez remains winless in six LaLiga games against Barcelona (D1 L5), and he may not have had a better chance of ending that stretch here. But the Blaugrana will feel they were worthy winners, having registered 3.22 expected goals from 29 shots, while the visitors' four attempts were worth a combined 0.16 xG.
